s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal mass with hypertension and dizziness
salient_findings: Hypoechoic lesion with clear boundary between spleen and abdominal aorta
Smoothly marginated soft-tissue mass in gastric wall with marked enhancement
Submucosal elevation on gastric fundus with heterogeneous mass arising from muscularis propria
key_facts: 64-year-old woman with 20-year history of hypertension
Presenting with dizziness and head discomfort for 3 days
Blood pressure at presentation was 190/100 mmHg
No gastrointestinal symptoms
Abdominal ultrasound revealed 4.7 cm × 4.4 cm hypoechoic lesion
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed 5.5 cm × 4.3 cm smoothly marginated soft-tissue mass
Upper endoscopy revealed smooth, hemispherical submucosal elevation on gastric fundus
Endoscopic ultrasonography demonstrated 3.7 cm × 4.4 cm hypoechoic, heterogeneous mass
EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration obtained scant gastric mucosal tissue and few spindle cells
Vital signs were within normal limits
Physical examination was unremarkable
Routine blood tests, blood biochemistry, fecal occult blood, and tumor markers were all normal

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Incidentally revealed hypoechoic lesion with clear boundary, suggested by radiologist to originate from the stomach

shortlist.label: Leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Smooth, hemispherical submucosal elevation on gastric fundus, consistent with a benign tumor

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypoechoic, heterogeneous mass arising from the muscularis propria, raising concern for a malignant tumor

shortlist.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal elevation and heterogeneous mass, although less likely given the lack of gastrointestinal symptoms

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Spindle cell tumor with areas of calcification, a possible diagnosis given the EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration findings

raw.rationale: The presence of a hypoechoic, heterogeneous mass arising from the muscularis propria with spindle cells on EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration, along with the location and characteristics of the mass, supports the diagnosis of a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST).

rejected.label: Leiomyoma
rejected.why: While leiomyoma could present as a submucosal mass, the presence of spindle cells with areas of calcification and the size of the mass are more suggestive of a malignant process like GIST.

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: Similar to leiomyoma, leiomyosarcoma is a consideration, but the specific findings and location are more characteristic of GIST.

rejected.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The absence of gastrointestinal symptoms and the nature of the mass (arising from the muscularis propria, hypoechoic, and heterogeneous) are not typical for gastric adenocarcinoma, which usually arises from the mucosa.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: While schwannoma could present as a submucosal mass, the specific characteristics and the presence of spindle cells with calcification are more indicative of GIST, especially given the location and the patient's presentation.
